description: Desktop-only capability. Filesystem access is scoped to the preferences file, using the same six bare command permissions as the shared capability and the same reason: the permission SETS (`fs:allow-app-read` / `fs:allow-app-write`) are `["read-all"|"write-all", "scope-app"]`, and tauri-utils' ACL resolver UNIONS a permission set's own scope with the capability's `allow` list rather than intersecting them (acl/resolved.rs does `resolved_scope.allow.extend(allow)` for both). Granting the set therefore gave the WebView create/copy/remove/rename/truncate/write plus readDir/stat/watch over every top-level path in $APPDATA, $APPCONFIG, $APPCACHE and $APPLOG — not "the preferences file", which is what the previous description here claimed. No opener permission is granted: the app calls its own `open_external_url`, which uses the plugin's Rust API and is not ACL-gated, so `opener:default` (which includes the unused `allow-reveal-item-in-dir`) was dead weight.
